Strategy Guide & Success Criteria

Learn how to optimize your solutions for different towns and disaster scenarios

Understanding Success

Excellent

+1 to +20

Your solutions completely overcome the disaster and improve the community

Good

-4 to 0

Significant impact reduction with minimal remaining deficit

Fair

-9 to -5

Some improvement but more solutions needed

Poor

-10 or worse

Disaster impact remains severe

Town-Specific Optimization Strategies

Havenwood - The River Town

Vulnerabilities

  • • Historic downtown lacks modern building codes
  • • River flooding poses constant threat
  • • Aging infrastructure throughout
  • • Remote location affects response times

Optimal Solutions

  • • Levee & Floodwall Upgrades - Essential for flood scenarios
  • • Smart Building Codes - Cost-effective infrastructure improvement
  • • Public Safety Campaign - Builds trust in tight-knit community
  • • Emergency Supply Stockpile - Critical for remote access issues

Port St. Jude - The Economic Hub

Vulnerabilities

  • • Dense urban development increases risk
  • • Critical port infrastructure
  • • Industrial facilities create multiple hazards
  • • Large population requires extensive resources

Optimal Solutions

  • • Seismic Retrofitting - Protects high-value infrastructure
  • • Modern Early Warning System - Essential for large population
  • • Utility Grid Hardening - Maintains economic operations
  • • Post-Disaster Relief Funds - Quick recovery for businesses

Whispering Pines - The Mountain Community

Vulnerabilities

  • • Extreme isolation affects emergency response
  • • Wildfire risk from forest proximity
  • • Single access road creates bottleneck
  • • Small population means limited resources

Optimal Solutions

  • • Defensible Space Program - Critical wildfire protection
  • • Emergency Supply Stockpile - Compensates for isolation
  • • Public Safety Campaign - Maximizes community self-reliance
  • • Modern Early Warning System - Early evacuation critical

Advanced Optimization Tips

Resilience vs Trust Balance

  • • High Resilience Focus: Choose infrastructure solutions (Design category)
  • • High Trust Focus: Prioritize community solutions (Response category)
  • • Balanced Approach: Mix both categories for optimal outcomes
  • • Emergency Situations: Trust often recovers faster than infrastructure

Managing Random Modifiers

  • • Diversify Solutions: Don't put all budget into one category
  • • Build Buffer: Account for potential negative modifiers
  • • Multiple Projects: Spread risk across several solutions
  • • Community Focus: Trust-building solutions are more stable

Cost-Effectiveness Analysis

  • • Best Value: Smart Building Codes (6 resilience + 2 trust = 8 total for $3M)
  • • Trust Champions: Public Safety Campaign & Relief Funds
  • • Resilience Champions: Levee Upgrades & Early Warning Systems
  • • Avoid: Single high-cost solutions without support

Common Optimization Mistakes

  • • Over-engineering: Spending entire budget on one solution
  • • Ignoring Trust: Technical solutions without community buy-in
  • • Wrong Disaster Match: Not tailoring to specific scenario
  • • Town Mismatch: Ignoring local vulnerabilities and strengths
